metadata.methods_description: Each session comprised 50 trials (2 practice, 48 experimental). Each trial had two learning trials with guided navigation to an object, followed by one test trial with the object invisible. Half of the experimental trials were stimulated, with stimulation lasting 5 s during both associated learning trials. Stimulation was delivered to a single electrode at a time, and its parameters are recorded in the events files. Trial blocks were counterbalanced using reflected object and start positions. Recordings were made with Blackrock or Medtronic systems at multiple clinical sites.

citation_details.title: Brain state sets the spatial scale at which cortical geometry constrains human cortical dynamics
citation_details.author: Alejandro Salinas-Medina, Anisleidy González Mitjans, P.-J. Toussaint, Xue Liu, Alan Charles Evans
citation_details.abstract: Abstract How anatomy constrains large-scale cortical dynamics is contested. Two lines of evidence about what shapes large-scale cortical activity appear to conflict. One holds that geometric eigenmodes of the cortical surface explain brain function more parsimoniously than connectome-derived modes; another holds that long-range connections shape dynamics over and above geometry. We show that neither is categorically right, and that the disagreement dissolves once spatial scale is resolved: connectivity accounts for the broadest cortical patterns and histological geometry for the finer ones. Using cortico-hippocampal neural field models built on ultrahigh-resolution histological geometry and tested against human intracranial recordings and task fMRI, we identify a second constraint. Anatomical pathways are commonly treated as fixed contributions that operate similarly across brain states. Instead, the same hippocampal–entorhinal relay degrades cortical theta organisation during sleep yet supplies it during spatial navigation. Brain state changes the effective spatial scale at which cortical geometry is read out, so anatomy constrains cortical function only jointly with state.
